review_scope: interior_pilot uniform range claim, shared budget, partial-subdivision recovery

findings.title: Normal leader exit returns while same-group descendant continues beyond wall budget
findings.reproduction: Synthetic parent spawns a same-group Python child that sleeps .6 s then creates a sentinel; parent exits immediately. Call run_guarded with .2 s wall cap.
findings.impact: Guard reports PROCESS_COMPLETED while a non-escaped descendant still runs and mutates output after receipt. RLIMIT_AS and CPU caps are inherited but do not bound a sleeping descendant wall time. Single-process wording does not enforce rejection of this case.
findings.minimum_fix: On normal/nonzero leader completion and exception paths, detect/kill remaining process group before output snapshot and receipt. Record descendants cleanup or explicit single-process contract violation. Alternatively supervise group lifetime through the deadline with an appropriate Linux job boundary. Keep escaped-group exclusion and per-process memory disclaimer.

postfix_closure.verified: Guard rejects successful completion, sends remaining-group SIGKILL, and original delayed sentinel no longer appears. Finally-path group cleanup is present in inspected source.
postfix_closure.measurement_limit: killpg(pid,0) checks group existence, not runnable state; its true result may include zombies or pending termination. No fully-reaped process-tree claim.

verified_semantics: RLIMIT_AS is explicitly per-process virtual address space, not aggregate tree RSS.
RLIMIT_CPU and output RLIMIT_FSIZE are explicitly per-process/per-file; parent reads at most 65536 bytes per output preview.
Live-leader timeout sends SIGKILL to its process group.
RangeClaim structurally binds both whole integration panel and whole parameter rectangle, with uniform=True and a nonempty proof reference; callback truth remains externally proved.
Shared Budget counts nested evaluations and releases owned panel/state reservations on exit.
Exact endpoint replacement removes the same old endpoints; it does not interval-subtract an uncertain contribution.
A ResourceLimit during incomplete subdivision preserves the previously complete valid total; invalid/domain/implementation callback failures discard acceptance.
Nested toy callback supplies a uniform inner image over the full outer panel, independent of unused outer z, and safely accepts wide-but-valid inner enclosures.
Cooperative time and tracked-state memory are accurately distinguished from hard process caps.
source_artifacts_capture_note: The first hash capture for host_guard occurred after the concurrent root fix; its hash is the post-fix identity, not the identity of the earlier failing probe. The original failing behavior is preserved in the probe receipt and earlier source inspection; no pre-fix byte hash was captured.
